content:
Alex Carter: Observed a recurring failure mode: quant profiles generated for one model variant (rdx-13b) being applied to another (rdx-13b-v2 / rdx-14b) and causing silent quality regressions. Proposal: a portability/mapping layer that translates profiles across families using an architecture fingerprint + per-layer heuristics before applying. Ideas?
Priya Sharma: yeah we saw that in the last canary. curious what the fingerprint contains and how greedy the mapping should be. also, how do we avoid humans in the loop for every small update?
Mateo Ruiz: two parts: (1) a similarity score between source and target (activation distribution KL, layer shapes, relative head counts), (2) a mapping transform that adjusts scales and clamping thresholds. If similarity < threshold -> disallow auto-apply.
Casey Li: format suggestion for mapping artifact: simple JSON that references original profile id, source-fingerprint, target-fingerprint, and a small remap function represented as ops. Example:
```json
{
  "source_profile": "profile:rdx-13b-int8-2025-07-01",
  "source_fp": "sha256:abcd...",
  "target_fp": "sha256:ef01...",
  "layer_map": {"enc.layers.0.attn.q.k.scale":"enc.layers.0.attn.q.k.scale * 0.95"},
  "fallback": "profile:rdx-13b-int8-2025-07-01",
  "notes": "reduce head-scale by 5% on target due to observed activation shift"
}
```
Lana Gomez: ops: key risk is an automated remap that silently worsens p95 user metrics. We need a canary flow: apply to 0.5% warm traffic + evaluate on a wallet of prompts pre/post. rollback if delta > configured tolerance. Also add a hard cap on profile change magnitude per deploy.
Devon Park: automation idea: compute an "apply-safety" score = weighted(activation-KL, shape-compat, quant-sensitivity). If > 0.8 allow auto-translation; if 0.6-0.8 require human review, <0.6 block. This score can be trained from past rollout outcomes.
Jing Wu: telemetry: we must avoid sending any raw user text. activation stats must be aggregated histograms (bucketing) and hashed fingerprints only. Also keep privacy notes in the artifact.
Alex Carter: good call. Operational constraints: mapping artifacts should be immutable and stored alongside provenance (who generated, which calibration job, eval outcomes). We'll add a schema field for provenance with timestamps and eval-deltas.
Mateo Ruiz: validation harness: take the translated profile, run synthetic replay (no PII) across representative buckets: few-shot convo, code generation, long-context summarization. Metrics to log: delta-perplexity, delta-ROUGE, delta-accuracy (task-specific), and latency/cost change.
Casey Li: tie this into rollout controller: new field `max_profile_delta` that prevents >X% change in scale factors per-layer. Also `required_evals`: list of buckets that must pass with <threshold regression.
Lana Gomez: ops-bot can we add automatic monitoring alerts for rolled-out translations? ops-bot: yes, rollout-controller will create ephemeral dashboards: profile_translation/<translation-id> showing metric deltas, sampled failure traces (no text), and an auto-rollback switch.
ops-bot: Note: translations that trigger rollback more than twice will be quarantined and marked for manual forensic. See /infra/rollout/policy.
Devon Park: one subtlety: small architecture tweaks (e.g., layernorm epsilon change) can have outsized effects on FP8. We should include a per-op sensitivity fingerprint (e.g., LN-eps, gelu-variant) to bump similarity weighting.
Priya Sharma: practical ask: how do we bootstrap for new families that don't have source profiles? fallback is to run a fresh calibration job. But maybe we can prioritize hot-layer calibration (heads and first/last layers) to get a cheap partial profile.
Alex Carter: plan: (A) define fingerprint schema and mapping-JSON schema; (B) implement similarity scoring prototype in tools/quant-portability; (C) build validation harness and integrate with rollout controller; (D) docs and provenance. Owners: Casey (schema + rollout cap), Mateo (validation harness), Devon (similarity scoring), Lana (ops dashboards), Jing (privacy & telemetry).
Jing Wu: I'll add the privacy checklist and aggregation formats.
Casey Li: I'll draft the schema PR and a small contract for `max_profile_delta`.
Mateo Ruiz: starting notebook for validation harness, will post link when ready.
Lana Gomez: will schedule infra window to add ephemeral dashboards and alerts.
Alex Carter: I'll file the RFC follow-up referencing this thread: https://redwood.internal/r/quant-portability (WIP). If no objections, we'll start the prototype this week.
Priya Sharma: sounds good. also, let's remember to include a human-review path in the console for borderline translations.
Alex Carter: agreed. Thanks team :thumbsup:
